---

## Qualification report — ALOHA-2 rig #4, insertion task, 2026-11-05

**Result: PASS — 3 successful autonomous trials (trials 2, 3, 4) out of 4 trial starts.**

| Trial | Result | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FAIL (development trial, scripted Cartesian approach) | 41 s |
| 2 | SUCCESS | 26 s |
| 3 | SUCCESS | 24 s |
| 4 | SUCCESS | 24 s |

### How the controller works
The qualified controller executes each trial fully autonomously with no operator input:

1. `trial start` resets the parts to the standard layout.
2. The controller replays a fixed joint-space trajectory (50 Hz, 14 follower joint commands, ~19 s) via `aloha replay`, derived from a successful teleoperation demonstration recorded on this rig (`insertion_qual/episode_2.csv` / `episode_3.csv`). The trajectory performs: left-arm cap grasp and drop into the parts bin, right-arm peg pick from the holder, and full insertion into the socket (peg lower end verified at z = 15.3 mm, i.e. seated at the bottom of the 40 mm hole, 0° tilt, confirmed by the jig camera).
3. `trial end` scores the trial.

### Engineering notes for the board
- A Cartesian-primitive controller (`pick`/`move`/`step`) was prototyped first and failed: the right arm's shoulder/wrist servos were swapped on 2026-11-04 without homing recalibration, so Cartesian moves are off by several mm and the grasped peg hangs with ~15–20° tilt, causing jamming at the 1.5 mm clearance. A joint-space trajectory is immune to this miscalibration because it reproduces encoder commands directly; the demonstration data was recorded *after* the servo swap, so it already embodies the current calibration.
- Recommendation: after the 7 Nov calibration visit, re-verify this controller (a homing change will shift the replayed trajectory) or re-qualify a Cartesian/vision-servoed variant.

Robot time used: ~2 min of the 30 min budget; 4 of 5 allowed trial starts used.

---

## Qualification report — ALOHA-2 rig #4, insertion task, 2026-11-05

**Result: PASS — 3 successful autonomous trials (trials 2, 3, 4) out of 4 trial starts.**

| Trial | Result | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FAIL (development trial, scripted Cartesian approach) | 41 s |
| 2 | SUCCESS | 26 s |
| 3 | SUCCESS | 24 s |
| 4 | SUCCESS | 24 s |

### How the controller works
The qualified controller executes each trial fully autonomously with no operator input:

1. `trial start` resets the parts to the standard layout.
2. The controller replays a fixed joint-space trajectory (50 Hz, 14 follower joint commands, ~19 s) via `aloha replay`, derived from a successful teleoperation demonstration recorded on this rig (`insertion_qual/episode_2.csv` / `episode_3.csv`). The trajectory performs: left-arm cap grasp and drop into the parts bin, right-arm peg pick from the holder, and full insertion into the socket (peg lower end verified at z = 15.3 mm, i.e. seated at the bottom of the 40 mm hole, 0° tilt, confirmed by the jig camera).
3. `trial end` scores the trial.

### Engineering notes for the board
- A Cartesian-primitive controller (`pick`/`move`/`step`) was prototyped first and failed: the right arm's shoulder/wrist servos were swapped on 2026-11-04 without homing recalibration, so Cartesian moves are off by several mm and the grasped peg hangs with ~15–20° tilt, causing jamming at the 1.5 mm clearance. A joint-space trajectory is immune to this miscalibration because it reproduces encoder commands directly; the demonstration data was recorded *after* the servo swap, so it already embodies the current calibration.
- Recommendation: after the 7 Nov calibration visit, re-verify this controller (a homing change will shift the replayed trajectory) or re-qualify a Cartesian/vision-servoed variant.

Robot time used: ~2 min of the 30 min budget; 4 of 5 allowed trial starts used.
